name: text-to-cad
one_liner: Lets an AI coding assistant design real, manufacturable 3D parts from a text description, check if they can actually be made, and send them straight to a 3D printer or machine shop.
buyer: A product designer or mechanical engineer at a small hardware startup who wants to go from idea to printable part in minutes instead of days in CAD software.
business_use_cases: A small hardware startup uses it to rapid-prototype enclosures and brackets without hiring a dedicated CAD engineer.
A maker business generates custom-fit parts, like phone mounts or replacement clips, on demand from customer descriptions.
A repair shop designs one-off replacement parts for appliances and prints them same-day instead of sourcing discontinued parts.

money_ideas.idea: Run a 'describe it, we print it' custom part shop: customers describe what they need, the agent designs it, you 3D print and ship.
Offer a subscription CAD-assistant service for small manufacturers who need occasional custom tooling or jigs.

steal_this: This weekend, set up a simple web form where people describe a part they need, pipe it through text-to-cad, and quote them a price to print and ship it.
